mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of Taiwan corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Taiwan is not an Apostille state): notarize at Taiwan district court notary, certify at Taiwan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then complete SEF/ARATS cross-strait notarization verification; no Hague Apostille is chained or used.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for Taiwan corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (parallel non-Apostille path): Taiwan notarial certification, Taiwan MOFA authentication, and SEF/ARATS verification only; no Hague Apostille is applied.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for incorporation and capital subscription
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of Taiwan shareholder, notarized in Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization for non-member state: Taiwan notary public attestation of signatories and board minutes, Taiwan MOFA certification, then SEF/ARATS verification; never combined with apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of Taiwan corporate shareholder and latest amended charter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan company, certified by Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization: authenticated copy with Taiwan notary and MOFA, followed by SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification; Hague Apostille does not apply to Taiwan-origin instruments.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from Taiwan shareholder clearing bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization: banker signature notarized, bank license confirmed by Taiwan Banking Bureau, MOFA certification, then SEF/ARATS verification; no apostille is used.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO identification and beneficial owner declaration for Taiwan corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan notary public and shareholder directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization: individual identities notarized, MOFA certified, and SEF/ARATS verified; also filed in the PRC beneficial owner registry on a Government_Only_Access basis.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders, authorized signatories and senior family-office personnel against OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists (1267/1989/1988/2231), China Ministry of Public Security terrorism list, China MOFCOM export-control and sanction lists, EU and UK sanctions lists, and Taiwan FIU alerts. PEPs must be identified including domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members and close associates, with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation. Enhanced due diligence applies to the Taiwan investor and all downstream payment rails; adverse news, multi-jurisdictional sanctions overlays and ongoing transaction monitoring are mandatory for a single-family-office investment holding vehicle.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Name Registration and Reservation System via local Market Supervision Administration online registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official name must be in simplified Chinese script, not traditional Chinese. The four-tier statutory formula is administrative division, distinctive trade name, industry or business features, and limited liability company. English and pinyin are permitted only as supplementary transliteration, not as the registry name. For an ISIC 6430 SFO, the trade name must avoid financial or wealth-management indications; use a neutral industry label such as business management consulting or industrial investment holding.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, obtain the written rejection notice citing the specific clause of the PRC Administrative Measures for Enterprise Name Registration. File administrative reconsideration with the next higher-level SAMR within 60 days, or initiate an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court within six months. Simultaneously revise and resubmit the proposed name on the portal; if the rejection involves a sensitive token, obtain a no-objection letter from the competent ministry or financial regulator before appeal. Name reservations may be extended once for 30 days by applying before expiry; if no extension is obtained, the name is released and a fresh application may be filed immediately after a five-day cool-down period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Rejected. PRC Company Law requires a fixed business premise registered by SAMR. Virtual office, commercial mailbox and mail-forwarding addresses are not accepted by local tax authorities for VAT invoice registration and are rejected by banks for corporate account opening. incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan, Articles 128, 154, 156, 172, 183, 208, 218, and 387; Foreign Investment Act; Investment Commission review rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce - Company Registration Division and One-Stop Service
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application for a Foreign-Invested Limited Company
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for this limited company under the Company Act of Taiwan. The paid-up capital must be remitted into a bank account opened in the company's name in Taiwan and verified by a certified public accountant before submission to the registry. No blocked escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME], A WHOLLY FOREIGN-OWNED LIMITED COMPANY ORGANIZED UNDER THE COMPANY ACT OF TAIWAN. RESOLUTION NO. 2025-BOD-01. The first meeting of the board of directors of the Company was held on [date] at [address]. The following directors were present: [director A], [director B], and [director C], constituting a quorum. The chairperson opened the meeting and confirmed that the sole shareholder had duly appointed the above directors and that all corporate approvals required by the Foreign Investment Act had been obtained. After discussion, the following resolutions were unanimously adopted. 1. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. The authorised share capital of the Company shall be [amount] divided into [number] shares, and the paid-in share capital shall be [amount]. The sole shareholder, [name], is authorised and directed to subscribe for all issued shares, to pay the full subscription price in cash into a bank account opened in the name of the Company, and to retitle such contribution as paid-in capital. The board ratifies the subscription allotment and directs the officers to obtain the required capital verification report. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company shall be located at [address], which shall be the statutory seat for service of process, tax notices, and official communications. The chairperson is authorised to execute the lease, undertake fit-out and safety compliance, and notify the competent authority of any change. 3. BANKING AUTHORISATION. The board authorises the Company to open banking, custody, and brokerage accounts at [financial institution]. [Officer A] and [Officer B] are designated as authorised signatories; any two designated signatories together shall sign for transactions exceeding [amount]. The officers are authorised to execute account mandates, electronic-banking agreements, and investment instructions consistent with the single-family office investment policy. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. [Name] is appointed chairperson and managing director; [Name] is appointed company secretary; [Name] is appointed chief financial officer and principal accounting officer. Each officer shall have the powers and duties set by the Articles, the Company Act, and this resolution. The secretary shall maintain minutes, the share register, and statutory filings; the chief financial officer shall administer treasury, custody, books, and accounts. 5. IMPLEMENTATION. The chairperson and secretary, jointly or singly, are authorised to prepare, sign, notarise, and file the Articles of Incorporation, incorporation application, tax registration, and any ancillary documents, to engage counsel and certified public accountants, and to pay reasonable pre-incorporation expenses. All acts taken pursuant to this resolution are ratified, and the next board meeting shall receive a full report. This resolution is binding on all officers and shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign investment approval and pre-incorporation name clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Investment Commission (online single-window portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application to the MOEA Investment Commission for approval of the proposed foreign investment, corporate name, and single-family office business scope. The application packet should identify all ultimate beneficial owners, provide proof of the foreign investor's legal existence, and include a two-year operating budget showing sources of funds and projected treasury activities. After provisional approval, the investor should reserve the registered address and open a preliminary banking channel before the notarization stage. A complete ownership chart and AML source-of-funds statement must accompany the filing to avoid an enhanced-review inquiry.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation of the foreign investor
Board resolution of the foreign investor authorizing the Taiwan entity
Audited financial statements or bank credit reference
Proposed company name in English and Chinese
Two-year operating budget and source-of-funds statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a deficiency notice, submit supplemental documents within 30 days. A refusal may be challenged by an administrative appeal to the Executive Yuan within 30 days after the written decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and execution of Articles of Incorporation and governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notarization office or licensed notary public in the execution jurisdiction, recognized by the MOEA Investment Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft bilingual Articles of Incorporation, shareholder consent resolution, and organizational meeting records in accordance with the approved business scope and capital structure. The foreign shareholder must execute the Articles and the first director consent letter before a notary or an equivalent authorized officer. The notary must certify copies of the parent company resolutions and verify the authority of the signing representatives. If the instruments are signed outside Taiwan, the authenticated signature chain must be completed through the relevant consulate or apostille procedure, and the clean notarized package must be delivered to the local attorney or formation agent.
required_dossiers: Notarized registered-office lease or owner consent letter
Power of attorney appointing local formation agent
Certified corporate identity and passport copies of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization or legalization is challenged, re-execute before a recognized notary or obtain a supplementary legal opinion. A defective stamp or seal may be corrected without re-filing if the registrar accepts an affidavit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Paid-in capital remittance and statutory CPA capital verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated foreign exchange bank and a Taiwan-certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a capital deposit account in the name of the soon-to-be-formed company at a designated foreign exchange bank, subject to the Investment Commission approval and an enhanced know-your-customer review. The foreign investor must remit the full subscribed capital via wire, clearly referencing the company name and the approved investment case number, and must obtain an inward remittance certificate and a bank confirmation letter. A Taiwan-certified public accountant must then examine the remittance advice, bank statement, shareholder subscription list, and the board minutes, and issue a formal capital verification report confirming that the paid-in capital is fully deposited and not borrowed or repatriated before registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of deposit issued in the company's name
Bank account mandate and signatory resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank flags the remittance for AML reasons, provide the source-of-funds evidence and the investor's audited financial statements. If the CPA report is not accepted, ask the CPA to amend and reissue the report; no new capital remittance is needed if the funds remain intact.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company registration filing with the MOEA Department of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commerce - Company Registration One-Stop Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete establishment registration package with the MOEA Department of Commerce through the Company Registration One-Stop Service, either by the licensed agent or an authorised representative. Attach the notarized Articles, the CPA capital verification report, the Investment Commission approval letter, the registered-office consent or lease, the director and supervisor consent forms, the shareholder ledger, and the fee payment receipt. The registrar will examine the legal form and capital evidence and, if satisfactory, issue the certificate of incorporation and a company registration number. After issuance, request the tax registration number and the corporate seal certification as necessary; the company becomes a legal person on issuance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA registrar queries the filing, respond within the stated cure period with corrected forms. If the registration is refused, file a formal petition with the MOEA and then an administrative appeal within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation tax, labor, and operational registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance, local municipal tax office, Labor Insurance Bureau, and corporate seal registration counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After certificate issuance, file the profit-seeking enterprise tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau and obtain the uniform serial number for future tax and electronic-invoice filing. Register as an employer with the Labor Insurance Bureau and National Health Insurance Administration if any employees are engaged, and complete municipal business tax filings, fire safety declarations for office premises, and corporate seal registration. Open operational bank, custody, and brokerage accounts under the board mandate, and notify the Investment Commission of any later capital or scope amendment. The single-family office should also adopt AML compliance policies consistent with the medium-risk enhanced due diligence classification.
required_dossiers: Company seal imprint and officer identification
Notarized registered-office lease or title document
Employer registration forms for labor and health insurance
Payroll records if any employees are hired
Bank account details for tax and operational purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office delays, use the provisional certificate to apply for bank accounts and account mandates. If the tax registration is rejected, correct the data and refile immediately, and request a review of any penalty.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial or manufacturing regulator has jurisdiction over this investment-holding entity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - this single-family office does not require a manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehouse operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA report or environmental registration is triggered by treasury and portfolio holding activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste streams are generated by this single-family office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no industrial premises, fire permit, structural load inspection, or hazardous operations clearance is required. The office should nevertheless maintain standard fire-safety measures and general workplace occupational safety, and the landlord s fire certificate should be kept on file.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (財政部), Taxation Administration (賦稅署); National Taxation Bureau (國稅局) for national tax registration and assessment. E-Tax Portal: https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw; Ministry of Finance: https://www.mof.gov.tw.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Taiwan-incorporated WFOE must: (1) obtain foreign-investment approval from the Investment Commission, MOEA, and complete company registration; (2) upon incorporation, apply to the competent National Taxation Bureau for taxpayer registration and obtain the Uniform Invoice Number (統一編號, UIN), which serves as the statutory TIN/VAT ID; (3) receive the Business Tax Registration Certificate; (4) complete payroll withholding and entity registration; (5) for an SFO with only investment holding activities, no separate license is required; the same UIN is used for corporate income tax, business tax, and e-invoice filings. Non-resident foreign enterprises without a fixed place of business may request a withholding tax TIN directly from the National Taxation Bureau.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan has no 'check-the-box' or pass-through election. A WFOE is per se taxable as a profit-seeking enterprise. Available elections include: (i) foreign income tax credit election for foreign-source income under Income Tax Act Article 3; (ii) inter-corporate dividend exclusion election under Article 42; (iii) election to use cost-average or specific identification for securities sales for an SFO holding assets; and (iv) application for advance rulings/APAs. Hybrid mismatch structures are constrained by the controlled-foreign-enterprise and general anti-avoidance rules (Income Tax Act Article 43-3), so hybrid mismatch elections are not permissible.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Business Tax (Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act; commonly VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$200,000 average monthly sales. Above this threshold, a business must register as a full VAT taxpayer and issue Uniform Invoices; below the threshold, it is a 'small-scale business' subject to a 1% business tax on gross sales, but is still required to register and file returns.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Full VAT registrants must issue Uniform Invoices (統一發票). Electronic Uniform Invoices (E-Invoices) are mandatory for qualifying businesses and must be transmitted in real time through the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Integration Platform using the Turnkey API gateway; digital stamping and encryption are applied to each invoice. There is no per-invoice administrative clearance, but real-time synchronization enables automated audit scrutiny and data matching.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rating applies when tangible goods are actually exported from the Taiwan area and the exporter holds an approved customs export declaration (出口報單) and shipping evidence. Services: zero-rating applies to services provided to a foreign client or for exclusive use outside Taiwan, provided the service is not treated as domestic use, the consideration is externally sourced, and the supplier retains documentation showing the offshore destination; the burden of proving offshore use is on the taxpayer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate (匯入匯款通知書)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau may re-audit zero-rating claims within the statutory 5-year assessment period (7 years for fraud). Fraudulent or fictitious export claims trigger: (i) recollected output VAT at the standard 5% or higher; (ii) a penalty equal to five times the amount evaded under Business Tax Act Article 51; (iii) monetary fines under the Tax Collection Act; and (iv) criminal liability for willful tax evasion. Retrospective clawbacks include refunded input VAT plus interest and possible cancellation of the enterprise's e-invoice credentials.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China collectively exercise all FX administration, cross-border payment monitoring, and capital-account approval authority over the onshore WFOE. On the Taiwan side, the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) and the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) regulate the Taiwan-resident shareholder's outward remittance, including the applicable NT/USD conversion and cross-border transfer declaration thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CNY is fully convertible for current-account items subject to authenticity and consistency review by the designated FX bank, but remains a regulated, registration-based regime for capital-account items. For the WFOE, inbound equity capital (FDI) requires a SAFE foreign-exchange business registration (direct bank-underwriting model) before the capital-account receipt is credited; proceeds may be retained as FX or voluntarily settled into CNY subject to the negative list. Profit remittance to the Taiwan shareholder is treated as a current-account dividend and requires: (1) annual statutory audit confirming the existence of distributable profits, (2) corporate income tax clearance and 10% treaty-based withholding tax settled under the Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation and Tax Cooperation, subject to the Taiwan shareholder satisfying beneficial-ownership and Taiwan tax-residency conditions, and (3) SAFE dividend remittance verification executed by the sponsor bank. The principal remaining hurdles are the capital-account negative list, which prohibits capital-settled CNY from being used for downstream equity investment, securities investment, entrusted loans, or wealth-management products unless a specific pilot-zone permission is obtained, and the strict 'real transaction' verification applied to each dividend remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The former statutory export-collection-verification deadline of 180 days was repealed in 2012 and replaced by the SAFE Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring and Aggregate Verification system under the 'Administrative Measures for Foreign Exchange in Trade' (SAFE Document HuiFa[2012] No. 38, as amended). Under the current regime, all trade current-account FX receipts must be repatriated to a licensed domestic bank within each enterprise's declared expected collection date recorded on the Trade FX Monitoring System; a 90-day benchmark applies for standard open-account general exports and up to 180 days for documentary collection/letters of credit, with any extension requiring substantiation and possible A-list downgrade to B/C-list status. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; the former mandatory surrender obligation has been repealed and the exporter may retain receipts in a trade-FX account or freely convert into CNY at market rates. For the subject SFO/WFOE, registered as an investment-holding vehicle under ISIC 6430, no active trade-FX directory status is required; the entity must report the absence of export performance and maintain no idle trade receipts, and any incidental export proceeds would immediately trigger the repatriation and monitoring obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment_appen: The Taiwan shareholder side is separately governed by CBC regulations for outward remittance; the proposed dividend and capital-increase flows should be structured as standing, document-backed corporate remittances with the Taiwan remitting bank holding the PRC tax withholding certificate and SAFE verification forms to avoid 'Form S' document escalation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for onshore domestic clearing and capital-account transactions; Moderate for ancillary cross-border trade-collection facilitation under a SAFE-registered payment-institution pilot. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, PingPong, Currenxie, Wise Business) hold no PRC banking licence, cannot open or host the WFOE's regulatory accounts, cannot receive the registered-capital escrow, and cannot replace the SAFE business-registration conformity check. Their permissible use is confined to genuine goods-trade collection corridors supervised by a licensed onshore payment institution, with final RMB clearing forced back into a regulated bank account. The treasury blueprint mandates BOC and CMB as the sole sponsor banks for capital-account and dividend flows; an EMI may be used only as a non-material auxiliary conduit for cross-border e-commerce receivables and must never be referenced in any SAFE E-form or capital-account instruction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance at a bank counter is mandatory for the legal representative or the authorized officer holding a board resolution and a notarized power-of-attorney to open any foreign-currency-capable account and the capital escrow account. Remote video-based account opening is permitted only for basic RMB operational accounts in designated PBOC pilot zones, and even then dual-video recording and a subsequent on-site branch visit or verification interview are generally required. For a Taiwan-invested SFO/WFOE, branch-level compliance will additionally require enhanced ultimate-beneficial-ownership interviews, source-of-wealth explanations, and a physical site inspection of the registered office; a shared-office or virtual-address registration materially increases the probability of a site visit and document production order.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Family-office purpose with no operating revenue and zero onshore employees, presenting as a pure investment-holding shell.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements since incorporation; board resolution describing the group treasury and asset-preservation mandate; office lease and utility contracts; employment contracts or a duly executed service agreement with an outsourcing firm; business plan demonstrating restriction of investment activity to the family's own assets with no third-party capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Taiwan-resident ultimate beneficial owner combined with multi-layer offshore SPV or trust holding structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized or certified constitutional documents of each SPV layer; trust deed or will if a trust is interposed; chain-of-title share certificates; source-of-wealth and net-worth statements for each material beneficial owner; Taiwan tax-residency certificates; bank reference letters from the Taiwan parent's historical relationship bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large lumpy inbound capital injection funded in a single tranche without an operational rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Validated SAFE FDI business registration form (FDI E-form); business license and articles of association; board resolution approving the capital contribution; source-of-funds tracing file prepared by the Taiwan remitting bank; a capital-deployment schedule aligned with the SFO's stated investment-holding purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected unlicensed fund-management activity triggered by the ISIC 6430 family-office classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formal legal opinion confirming exemption from the PRC private-fund-management licensing regime because the vehicle serves a single family, does not pool external investor capital, and charges no management fee; constitutive documents showing the investment committee is restricted to family members; intra-group services agreement confirming that fee-bearing services are corporate treasury or administrative services, not collective asset management.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent related-party outbound payments to Taiwan or Hong Kong, including management fees and dividends, creating a payment-pattern red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed service agreements supported by transfer-pricing benchmarking; tax recordal certificates issued under the service-trade outward-remittance taxation filing process; board minutes authorizing each payment; payroll and HR records evidencing services received; VAT/fiscal invoices matching the nature and timing of each remittance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Step 1: Complete SAMR business licensing for the WFOE and open the basic deposit account at the chosen sponsor bank. Step 2: Complete the SAFE FDI business registration directly at the receiving bank under the bank-direct model and obtain the FDI Business Registration Certificate containing the E-form verification code. Step 3: Open the Foreign-Exchange Capital Account (CAPI) at the designated branch of BOC or CMB; the bank will reference the E-form, not a separate SAFE approval file. Step 4: The Taiwan shareholder remits via SWIFT MT103 with Field 70 including the FDI registration certificate number and the stated remittance purpose 'investment in registered capital', matching SAFE purpose code 622; the remitter must be the registered investor itself, and third-party payer wires will be rejected or placed on hold. Step 5: The receiving bank authenticates the wire against the FDI registration and credits the CAPI; proceeds can remain in USD or be settled into CNY under the 'voluntary settlement' rule into a dedicated settlement-pending-payment account. Step 6: Disbursement from the settlement-pending account is confined to the WFOE's legal business scope; if the family office intends to deploy capital-settled CNY into downstream onshore equity investments, a specific pilot-zone approval or separate compliance path must be obtained before settlement. Step 7: Every disbursement requires supporting contracts, VAT/fiscal invoices, and the bank-filed payment-submission form in the FX monitoring system.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For goods trade, the standard rails are SWIFT MT103/MT202 through the sponsor bank supported by the customs declaration and Trade FX Directory conformity; documentary settlements are executed through Irrevocable Letters of Credit (MT700 issued by BOC or CMB and advised by a Taiwan bank) with USD cleared via CHIPS and CNH cleared via the Taipei RMB Clearing Bank (Bank of China Taipei Branch) under the Cross-Strait RMB settlement mechanism. For services and related-party fees, the mandatory 'tax recordal for cross-border service-trade payments' must be electronically filed for payments equal to or exceeding the USD 50,000 equivalent, and the bank will not release the wire unless the tax recordal certificate and, where applicable, withholding tax payment vouchers are presented; royalties to Taiwan licensors must be cleared against withholding tax first. Dividend remittances follow the same SWIFT infrastructure but require audited annual financial statements, the dividend resolution, a confirmation of distributable profits, the corporate income tax settlement certificate, the 10% withholding tax certificate, and the SAFE current-account payment verification form before the MT103 can be released. As TWD is not a settlement currency in mainland China, the WFOE should convert CNY to USD or HKD for onward TWD conversion at the Taiwan beneficiary bank; a funded USD operational account at the sponsor bank is recommended to reduce FX-timing friction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY foreign-exchange forwards (yuan forward contracts) with documented real trade or capital-account background under the 'real demand' principle.
Onshore CNY foreign-exchange swaps between CNY and USD, EUR, or HKD for short-term liquidity management and rollover alignment.
Onshore cross-currency interest-rate swaps matched to an underlying term exposure of the WFOE's assets or liabilities.
Plain-vanilla CNY options on a covered basis, including risk-reversal structures, subject to bank approval and real-demand verification of the notional.
Offshore RMB non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed only by the Taiwan or other offshore parent treasury; NDFs are not permissible as an onshore instrument for the WFOE itself.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval and filing of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (Department of Commercial Affairs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval within 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., by June 30 for calendar-year companies); filing with MOEA within 15 days after approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file attracts a fine of NT$10,000–NT$50,000 per instance and an order to file; continuing default may lead to repeated fines and refusal of subsequent corporate registration applications.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (Company Public Information Registration System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every year by March 31; any change in directors, supervisors, managers, or shareholders holding 10% or more must be reported within 15 days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance or false declaration is punishable by a fine of NT$50,000–NT$500,000; after an order to correct, the fine may be imposed repeatedly until compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance, local district branch)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 through May 31 of the following tax year (calendar-year basis)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 1.15% monthly surcharge on the unpaid tax plus interest; prolonged failure to file can result in an assessed tax on an estimated basis and fines of up to 15% of the underpaid tax for non-deliberate cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Companies with paid-in capital of NT$30 million or more, or whose paid-in capital exceeds the threshold prescribed by the Ministry of Economic Affairs, must have annual financial statements audited and certified by a CPA. Smaller investment holding entities may submit unaudited statements but must still reconcile to tax-basis accounts for the annual income tax return.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (T-FRS), which are substantially converged with IFRS. Private companies not publicly traded may apply the Taiwan SME Accounting Standards; tax adjustments are required when the financial statements are used as the basis for the profit-seeking enterprise income tax filing.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Article 22-1 of the Taiwan Company Act, the WFOE must annually declare, by March 31, the names and details of directors, supervisors, managers, and all shareholders holding 10% or more of the shares. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the MOEA within 15 days. No separate annual certificate is issued unless a change occurs; the annual declaration itself constitutes the ongoing UBO confirmation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% flat rate of profit-seeking enterprise income tax (Income Tax Act, effective 2018 onwards) on net taxable income; an Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT) of 12% applies to the excess over NT$500,000 of the basic income base.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Domestic inter-corporate dividend exemption (Art. 42): dividends received by the Taiwanese WFOE from resident operating subsidiaries are excluded from taxable income, enabling tax-free upstream distributions, subject to AMT check; retained earnings surtax of 5% on undistributed surplus (reduced to 3% under the 2025 amendment) incentivizes full annual distribution to family shareholders; R&D and industrial innovation credits are generally unavailable to a pure holding SFO.
